processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The cylindrical sample (F 8 mm × 12 mm) was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s.
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 950 °C at a rate of 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set T before compression so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant strain-rate compression at 950 °C and 0.1 s^-1 to 60% reduction (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down (quenching), as also shown in figure_002.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (pre-deformation) microstructure of the as-forged FeeMneAleC steel: large polygonal grains delimited by a bright, continuous etched boundary network, with dark grain interiors containing abundant fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations/lamellae (dendritic/interdendritic segregation banding). Chemical heterogeneity is present in the as-forged condition.

phases_present.morphology: large polygonal grains with fine parallel lamellar striations (segregation banding)
phases_present.grain_size: individual grains span roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: large grains spanning roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar (no numeric value reported)

structures.overall_structure: After 60% hot compression the section parallel to the loading direction contains three deformation zones: 1 - difficult deformation zone, 2 - small deformation zone, 3 - large deformation zone. The degree of dynamic recrystallization (DRX) increases in the order zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation). With decreasing strain rate the recrystallized grains grow and microstructural heterogeneity improves; with increasing T the DRX volume fraction increases. The measured DRX grain size is taken from the core of the compressed sample (the large deformation zone).

microstructure_list.region: difficult deformation zone (zone 1, near loading surfaces)

phases_present.morphology: largest, least recrystallized grains; coarse grains (at higher T, few long straight boundaries)

microstructure_list.region: small deformation zone (zone 2, ends adjacent to horizontal centre line)

phases_present.morphology: intermediate between zones 1 and 3; banded/elongated remnant original grains with locally fine recrystallized grains at lower T

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (zone 3, central band / specimen core)

phases_present.morphology: region of greatest DRX; fine equiaxed recrystallized grains; at high strain rate serrated boundaries with small necklace-type DRX grains along elongated original boundaries, becoming uniform equiaxed with increasing T

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: This sample (950 °C/0.1 s^-1) lies within the hot-working window 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 in which sufficient dynamic recrystallization and a relatively fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained.

characterization_methods.technique: isothermal constant strain rate hot compression test
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900-1150 °C (this sample 950 °C), ε̇ = 0.01-10 s^-1 (this sample 0.1 s^-1), maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92)
characterization_methods.purpose: Acquire rheological (flow stress) curves to analyse hot deformation behavior, DRX activation energy, Z parameter and characteristic stress/strain values.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Flow stress decreases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (negative temperature-sensitive, positive strain rate-sensitive); a stress peak and subsequent softening are observed, indicating DRX.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; ground, polished and etched with 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction); 100 µm scale-bar micrographs of the three deformation zones.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe and analyse the microstructure evolution and DRX grain structure of the steel after hot compression.
characterization_methods.key_findings: DRX degree greatest in the large deformation zone (zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1); DRX volume fraction and grain size increase with T and with decreasing ε̇.

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic sine constitutive analysis (linear regression of lnε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)] and ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fit based on peak stress data over T = 900-1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01-10 s^-1.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The non-parallel fitted lines indicate deformation conditions notably affect the activation energy, so the calculated value is only the average within the experimental range.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates strain rate, peak stress and temperature: ε̇ = A[sinh(ασp)]^n exp(-Qp/RT)
analytical_models.model_note: Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2 (Eq. 2); Qp reported as average over the experimental range.

computational_details.simulation_method: Cingara-McQueen equation and Poliak-Jonas inflection-point analysis to determine the critical strain/stress for DRX
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Material constant C obtained by fitting ln(σ/σp) vs [ln(ε/εp)+1-ε/εp]; C = 0.1461 at 1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1 (R = 0.9728); obtained for all other T and ε̇.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The resulting εc/εp ≈ 0.452 agrees with literature values from the θ-σ inflection-point method, indicating the method is reliable.

analytical_models.model_note: Example fit at 1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1 with R = 0.9728; Eq. 9 gives εc/εp = [√(1-C)-(1-C)]/C ≈ 0.452.

computational_details.simulation_method: Zener-Hollomon parameter model with characteristic-value regression
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Computed over T = 900-1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01-10 s^-1; lnZ values tabulated in Table 1 (this sample 950 °C/0.1 s^-1 has lnZ = 63.58).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Z increases with ε̇ and decreases with T, matching the flow-stress trend; regression fits of σc/εc, σp/εp and σs/εs vs lnZ give R between 0.911 and 0.957.

analytical_models.equation_role: Multiple linear regression of DRX characteristic values on lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Used to construct the DRX state diagram (Fig. 7: A work hardening, B partial DRX, C complete DRX).

computational_details.simulation_method: Regression of DRX average grain size (Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation) and DEFORM-3D finite element simulation
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM-3D finite element software (Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation algorithm for regression)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Experimental data from 60% hot compression over T = 900-1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01-10 s^-1; billet rigid-plastic, die rigid with material parameters, semi-symmetric specimen, shear friction 0.3, billet-air convection coefficient 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation matched the thermal compression conditions.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%; absolute error between predicted and experimental grain size mostly within 3 µm.

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size model (Eq. 11, general)
analytical_models.model_note: Initial grain size and strain taken as fixed; ad0^hε^p treated as a constant.

analytical_models.model_name: Fitted DRX average grain size model (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.model_note: Validated in Fig. 11: R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53%, absolute error mostly < 3 µm. Applies to all hot-compression conditions including 950 °C/0.1 s^-1.

unmapped_findings: Zener-Hollomon parameter for the 950 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition: lnZ = 63.58 (Table 1).
Dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel: Qp = 669.844 kJ/mol (average value within the 900-1150 °C, 0.01-10 s^-1 experimental range; from Eq. 1-3).
Material constants from the constitutive analysis: stress level factor α = 0.00599, average slopes k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690.
Critical-to-peak strain ratio for DRX initiation: εc/εp ≈ 0.452 (from the Cingara-McQueen analysis).

No flow-stress, peak-stress, characteristic strain/stress or DRX grain-size value is reported specifically for the 950 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition; the peak-stress values quoted in the text are for 0.01 s^-1 (305.4 MPa at 900 °C falling to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C, an 82% reduction) and for 10 s^-1 (a 73% reduction over the same temperature range).

The 950 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition is not individually imaged in Fig. 9 (whose 950 °C panel is at ε̇ = 1 s^-1); the DRX average grain size for this exact condition is not given numerically but the condition lies within the reported optimum fine-uniform-grain window 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 (Fig. 10 / Fig. 11).
For this condition the strain-rate ranking of DRX grain size is 0.01 s^-1 > 0.1 s^-1 > 1 s^-1 > 10 s^-1 at any given temperature, and grain size increases with temperature for every strain rate.

The paper states that the same FeeMneAleC steel batch/composition was tested under identical experimental conditions to confirm reproducibility, and reports that the described experimental phenomena have reproducibility.
